entries.author: teacher
entries.content: The issue was that mypy always rendered `TypeType` (the internal type for `type[X]`/`typing.Type[X]`) as `Type[...]` in reveal_type notes and error messages, even on Python 3.9+ where mypy otherwise uses lowercase builtin names (e.g. `tuple[...]` via `Options.use_lowercase_names()`). I fixed the root cause by making the formatting consistent with that existing option: `TypeStrVisitor.visit_type_type` in `mypy/types.py` (used for reveal_type/reveal_locals) and `format_type_inner` in `mypy/messages.py` (used for all other error messages) now emit `type[...]` when `use_lowercase_names()` is true and `Type[...]` otherwise. I applied the same conditional to the hardcoded `"Type[...]"` spellings in `unsupported_type_type` ("Cannot instantiate type ...") in messages.py, the `"Type[...] can't contain another Type[...]"` error in typeanal.py, and the "without an explicit \"Type[...]\" annotation" error in semanal.py. Verified with the issue's repro (now consistently `type[...]` on 3.9+, `Type[...]` on 3.8 and with `--force-uppercase-builtins`) and the full testcheck, testsemanal, testtypes, and relevant testpythoneval suites all pass.
